chunks: Samāʿah asked him about a man who instructed his servants to perform tamattuʿ. He said:
"It is incumbent upon him to offer the sacrifice on their behalf."

I said: "What if he gave them dirhams, and some of them offered the sacrifice while others kept the dirhams and fasted?" He said: "That has sufficed for them, and he has the choice; if he wishes, he may leave it."
He said: "And if he had instructed them and they fasted, that would have sufficed for them."

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: it was sufficient and valid in fulfilling the duty
key_terms.صَامَ: he fasted as an alternative act
key_terms.غِلْمَانَهُ: his servants or slave-boys under his authority
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُوا: to perform tamattuʿ hajj, combining ʿUmrah with hajj

ai.seo_question: If servants are ordered to perform tamattuʿ hajj, does their master have to provide the sacrifice, and can fasting suffice instead?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning servants instructed to perform tamattuʿ in hajj. It states that sacrifice may be undertaken on their behalf, and that fasting can also suffice in place of sacrifice, indicating flexibility in fulfilling this obligation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2897 - It was narrated that Sama'ah asked Imam (as) about a man who instructed his servants to perform Tamattu‘ (Umrah and Hajj combined).
Imam (as) said: "It is incumbent upon him to offer the sacrifice on their behalf."

I said: "What if he gave them dirhams, and some of them offered the sacrifice while others kept the dirhams and chose to fast?"
Imam (as) said: "It is sufficient for them, and he has the choice to leave it as is if he wishes."
Imam (as) further said: "If he had commanded them to fast instead, it would have sufficed for them."
